GAGE MEASUREMENT LOCATION AND MEASUREMENT PLANE — 49 CFR PART 213 (in force 2026-11-21)

1. GOVERNING PROVISION
49 CFR § 213.53(a) — Gage (Subpart C, Track Geometry). Verbatim text, as it appears in both the eCFR current text and the CFR 2025 annual edition (revision date 2025-10-01):

  "(a) Gage is measured between the heads of the rails at right-angles to the rails in a plane five-eighths of an inch below the top of the rail head."

The identical sentence is repeated verbatim at § 213.323(a) for Class 6, 7, 8 and 9 track (Subpart G). The same 5/8 in reference plane is carried into the frog guard-face gage footnotes at §§ 213.143 and 213.355 ("A line five-eighths of an inch below the top of the center line of the head of the running rail, or corresponding location of the tread portion of the track structure") and into the alinement chord definition at § 213.327 ("The ends of the chord shall be at points on the gage side of the outer rail, five-eighths of an inch below the top of the railhead").

2. WHERE GAGE IS MEASURED (ASK 2)
Gage is the transverse clear distance between the two rail heads, measured from the gage line of one rail to the gage line of the other — i.e., from the gage-side face of one rail head (the side facing track center) to the gage-side face of the opposite rail head. The measurement is taken at right angles to the rails (perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the rail at the point of measurement), not at right angles to the track centerline on curves, and not along the top surface of the rail.

In practice: the gage bar's two contact faces bear on the gage side of each rail head at the specified elevation, and the reading is the distance between those two gage lines. "Between the heads of the rails" excludes any measurement taken across the base/flange, across the field side, or across the running surface at the top of rail.

3. MEASUREMENT PLANE — DEPTH BELOW TOP OF RAIL HEAD (ASK 3)
The measurement plane is five-eighths of an inch below the top of the rail head:

  5/8 in = 0.625 in = 15.875 mm  (0.625 in x 25.4 mm/in)

Stated as a depth: 0.625 in (15.875 mm) vertically below the top of the rail head, on each rail, on both sides of the track. The offset is measured downward from the top of the rail head (top of rail / running surface) at the location of the measurement. It is a fixed, dimensioned offset prescribed by the rule — it is not derived from rail section, head width, or wear, and it is not scaled or adjusted for rail size.

Why the rule uses this plane: the rail head is not a sharp-edged rectangle; the head has a crown and a fillet radius at the gauge corner. A measurement taken at the top of rail is unstable and varies with head wear and with where on the crown the gauge contacts. Measuring 5/8 in down places the contact below the crown and below the gauge-corner fillet, on the near-vertical gauge face, giving a repeatable, wear-tolerant reference.

4. CLASS APPLICABILITY — SAME CONVENTION, DIFFERENT LIMITS
This is a measurement convention, so it is uniform across all track classes in Part 213: excepted track and Classes 1-5 (§ 213.53(a)) and Classes 6-9 (§ 213.323(a)) all use the same "between the heads of the rails, at right angles to the rails, in a plane 5/8 in below the top of the rail head" definition. Only the numeric gage LIMITS change with class (§ 213.53(b), § 213.323(b)):

  Excepted track     —  no minimum;  max 4 ft 10-1/4 in
  Class 1            —  min 4 ft 8 in; max 4 ft 10 in
  Class 2 and 3      —  min 4 ft 8 in; max 4 ft 9-3/4 in
  Class 4 and 5      —  min 4 ft 8 in; max 4 ft 9-1/2 in
  Class 6            —  min 4 ft 8 in; max 4 ft 9-1/4 in; max change of gage within 31 ft 3/4 in
  Class 7, 8         —  min 4 ft 8 in; max 4 ft 9-1/4 in; max change of gage within 31 ft 1/2 in
  Class 9            —  min 4 ft 8-1/4 in; max 4 ft 9-1/4 in; max change of gage within 31 ft 1/2 in

Those figures are transverse limits in feet-inches; they are dimensionally distinct from, and must not be confused with, the 0.625 in (5/8 in) vertical depth of the measurement plane. Nominal standard gage, 4 ft 8-1/2 in (56.5 in; 1435 mm), is also a transverse dimension measured at that same 5/8 in plane — it is not a separate measurement convention.

5. DATE-OF-FORCE DETERMINATION (ASK 1)
Applicability: Part 213 applies to "all standard gage track in the general railroad system of transportation" (§ 213.3(a)), with the exclusions in § 213.3(b) (e.g., plant railroad track not part of the general system). The measurement rule quoted above is the one that governs that track.

Text verification for 2026-11-21:
  (a) eCFR current text of § 213.53, fetched 2026-11-23 (two days after the target date), shows the quoted 5/8 in language — sha256 c2bbfde68769.
  (b) CFR 2025 annual edition, Title 49 vol. 4, part 213 (revision date 2025-10-01), § 213.53(a), shows the identical sentence — sha256 dc44ad94cf3f (PDF) / 257a5a2da36c (§ 213.53 XML).
  (c) § 213.323(a) XML from the CFR 2024 edition (rev. 2024-10-01) carries the identical sentence — sha256 95678a12aaa9.

Three separate vintages (2024 annual, 2025 annual, current-as-of-2026-11-23) all carry the same text. Because the source fetched after the target date shows no change, the text in force on 2026-11-21 is the quoted text; the only residual gap would be an amendment with an effective date of 2026-11-22 or 2026-11-23, which could not alter the rule in force on 2026-11-21 absent retroactive effect. § 213.53 carries no recent amendment note beyond its base text in the 2025 edition, and the last amendment note on the parallel Class 6-9 provision is 78 FR 16104 (Mar. 13, 2013), confirming long-term stability of this definition. Residual-risk closure step if a certified date-stamped copy is required: pull the eCFR point-in-time view for 2026-11-21 (Title 49, Part 213, § 213.53) and run a Federal Register search for documents amending "213.53" with effective dates in 2025-10-01 through 2026-11-21.

6. DISTINCTIONS TO AVOID IN APPLICATION
  - Gage vs. crosslevel/surface/warp/alinement: those are separate Subpart C requirements with their own conventions (§§ 213.327, 213.331, 213.332). The 5/8 in plane is the gage-measurement convention; alinement independently references the same 5/8 in plane for chord endpoints on the gage side of the outer rail, but the two measurements answer different questions.
  - Gage vs. frog guard-face gage: §§ 213.143 and 213.355 set guard check and guard face gage limits using a line 5/8 in below the top of the center line of the head of the running rail — same reference elevation, different quantity.
  - Top-of-rail crown vs. the 5/8 in plane: on head-worn or hollow-worn rail, "top of the rail head" is taken at the running surface at the measurement location; the 0.625 in offset is applied from that surface, not from an unworn profile or from the rail's original catalog height.

7. ONE-LINE ANSWER
Under 49 CFR 213.53(a) (and identically 213.323(a) for Classes 6-9), as in force on 2026-11-21, gage is measured between the heads of the rails — gage line to gage line — at right angles to the rails, in a plane 5/8 inch (0.625 in; 15.875 mm) below the top of the rail head.

# Determination — curved-track requirements and a 0.20° curve under 49 CFR Part 213

## 1. Answer

**No.** Under 49 CFR Part 213 as in force on 2026-11-21, the requirements specified for curved track **do not apply** to a curve of 0.20 degree. A 0.20° curve falls below the curvature threshold in the part's applicability clause, so it is treated as non-curved (effectively tangent) for purposes of every requirement the part specifies *for curved track*.

## 2. Governing text (the scope clause that controls this question)

Subpart A — General, **§ 213.14 Application of requirements to curved track**:

> Unless otherwise provided in this part, requirements specified for curved track apply only to track having a curvature greater than 0.25 degree.
>
> [78 FR 16100, Mar. 13, 2013]

Identical rule for high-speed track, Subpart G, **§ 213.313 Application of requirements to curved track**:

> Unless otherwise provided in this part, requirements specified for curved track apply only to track having a curvature greater than 0.25 degree.
>
> [78 FR 16104, Mar. 13, 2013]

Both were confirmed word-for-word in the eCFR text of Part 213 and in the 2025 and 2024 annual CFR editions of Title 49, Volume 4. The source note in every instance is 78 FR 16100 / 16104 (Mar. 13, 2013), i.e. the provision has not been amended since 2013.

### 2.1 Why § 213.14 is "the scope clause" here, and not § 213.1 or § 213.3

The part has three layers of applicability, and the engineer's question is answered at the third:

| Clause | Function | Does it decide the 0.20° question? |
|---|---|---|
| § 213.1 Scope of part | Says the part prescribes minimum safety requirements for railroad track that is part of the general railroad system of transportation; Subparts A–F apply to Classes 1–5, Subpart G to higher speeds | No — establishes that the part governs at all, not which curvature-specific requirements attach |
| § 213.3 Application | Says the part applies to all standard gage track in the general railroad system, with listed exclusions | No — subject-matter jurisdiction, not curvature |
| **§ 213.14 (and § 213.313 for Subpart G)** | **"Application of requirements to curved track"** — states the curvature threshold at which curved-track requirements attach | **Yes — this is the operative clause** |

§ 213.14 is literally titled "Application of requirements to curved track" and its operative words — "Unless otherwise provided in this part…" — are the exact qualifier the engineer's question carries. The question is therefore answered on its own terms by reading the clause back to the engineer.

## 3. Applying the clause to 0.20 degree

The clause attaches curved-track requirements **only** where curvature is **greater than 0.25 degree**. That is a strict inequality with a hard floor.

- Curvature at issue: **0.20 degree**
- Regulatory threshold: **0.25 degree**
- Test: is 0.20 > 0.25? **No.**
- Result: the condition precedent in § 213.14 is not satisfied, so no requirement "specified for curved track" in Part 213 applies to this curve.

**Boundary note (safety-relevant, get it right in the field):** the clause excludes a curve of *exactly* 0.25 degree as well, because the threshold is "greater than," not "at least." A curve must be steeper than 0.25° before curved-track requirements attach. Do not round 0.25 up to "applies" and do not round 0.20 up to 0.25.

**Geometric cross-check (chord definition, R = 50 / sin(D/2)):**

- D = 0.20° → R ≈ 28,648 ft (≈ 5.43 miles)
- D = 0.25° → R ≈ 22,919 ft (≈ 4.34 miles)

The 0.20° curve has the larger radius, consistent with it being flatter than the 0.25° threshold curve. Using the arc definition (R = 5729.578 / D) gives R ≈ 28,648 ft at 0.20°, indistinguishable for this purpose; the choice of degree-of-curve convention does not change the conclusion.

## 4. What the "unless otherwise provided in this part" qualifier does — and does not — do

The qualifier preserves any provision elsewhere in Part 213 that either (a) extends curved-track requirements to gentler curves, or (b) states its own curvature rule. Reviewed against the part as in force:

| Provision | What it provides | Effect on a 0.20° curve |
|---|---|---|
| § 213.14 / § 213.313 | Curved-track requirements attach only above 0.25° | **Controls — requirements do not attach** |
| § 213.4 Excepted track | Operations may continue without complying with Subparts B, C, D and E unless otherwise expressly stated | Narrows applicability generally; does **not** extend curved-track requirements to gentler curves |
| § 213.17 Waivers | Administrator may waive requirements case-by-case | Relief mechanism, not an applicability rule; and a waiver cannot be assumed — a granted waiver must be produced |
| § 213.9(a) speed-limit exceptions (cross-references to §§ 213.57(b), 213.59(a), 213.113(a), 213.137(b) and (c)) | Modify maximum allowable operating speeds in specific circumstances | Speed provisions only; no curvature threshold of their own that reaches below 0.25° |
| § 213.57(b), § 213.59 | Elevation limits, elevation runoff, and curve speed formula | These **are** requirements "specified for curved track"; § 213.14 gates them out at 0.20° |
| Subpart G (§§ 213.301–213.369) | Parallel high-speed regime, with its own § 213.313 | Same 0.25° threshold; same result |

No provision surfaced in the part states a curvature threshold lower than 0.25 degree, and none expressly extends curved-track requirements to track flatter than 0.25 degree. The qualifier therefore does not displace the general rule for a 0.20° curve.

**Completeness step still owed before this is written into a compliance document:** run a full-text search of the current Part 213 for "degree," "curvature," and "curve" and confirm no section outside those reviewed above sets a different threshold. On the text available, the answer is not in doubt; this step closes the negative on the qualifier.

## 5. What still applies to track laid on a 0.20° curve — do not over-read the answer

The verdict is narrow. § 213.14 gates only requirements **"specified for curved track."** Requirements of general applicability continue to apply to the same track, because they are not conditioned on curvature:

- **Still applies:** gage (§ 213.53), track alinement (§ 213.55), track surface (§ 213.63) including the crosslevel/warp limits that are written for track generally, combined alinement and surface deviations (§ 213.65), track structure (Subpart D), inspection (Subpart F), and the class speed limits of § 213.9.
- **Does not attach by reason of curvature:** the curve-specific elevation ceiling (§ 213.57(a)), the curve speed formula of § 213.57(b), and elevation/runoff requirements of § 213.59.

**Caution on mixed provisions.** Some generally applicable sections contain curve-specific rows or paragraphs (for example, the crosslevel-on-curves row of the § 213.63(a) table, and the cant-deficiency tables of § 213.63(b)). Read each such provision as two provisions: the tangent/general limits apply; the curve-specific limits are gated by § 213.14 and do not attach to a 0.20° curve. Do not carry a curve-specific limit onto this track, and do not drop the general limit because the curve-specific one is inapplicable.

**Practical consequence.** At 0.20° (≈ 28,648 ft radius) the curve is operationally indistinguishable from tangent for the purposes of Part 213's curve provisions. Speed over this segment is governed by the class limits of § 213.9, not by a curve-derived posted speed under § 213.57(b).

## 6. Currency as of 2026-11-21

- The eCFR text of Part 213 retrieved 2026-11-23 (two days after the target date) carries § 213.14 and § 213.313 verbatim as quoted, with source notes 78 FR 16100 and 78 FR 16104 (Mar. 13, 2013).
- The CFR 2025 annual edition (Title 49, Vol. 4) and the CFR 2024 annual edition carry the identical text.
- No amendment to either section appears in the surfaced material between 2013 and the retrieval date.
- Residual window: a final rule effective on or before 2026-11-21 but published after the 2025 annual edition would appear in the 2026-11-23 eCFR text; it does not. A rule with an effective date between 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-23 would be immaterial to the target date.

Conclusion: the quoted text is the text in force on 2026-11-21.

## 7. Recommended record for the engineer (one-paragraph determination to file)

> Track segment [ID], curvature 0.20 degree measured by [method / chord length / date / instrument]. Under 49 CFR 213.14 (Subpart A), requirements specified for curved track apply only to track having a curvature greater than 0.25 degree; 0.20 degree is not greater than 0.25 degree. Accordingly, the curved-track requirements of Part 213 (including §§ 213.57 and 213.59 and the curve-specific limits within §§ 213.55 and 213.63) do not apply to this segment. Generally applicable requirements of Part 213 — gage, alinement, surface, track structure, inspection, and the § 213.9 class speed limits — remain in force. No provision of Part 213 has been identified that provides otherwise. Determined by [name], [title], [date].

**Safety caveat to carry forward:** § 213.1(a) states that the requirements apply to specific track conditions existing in isolation and that a combination of conditions, none of which individually is a deviation, may still require remedial action for safe operations. The § 213.14 determination removes curve-specific obligations only; it is not a finding that the segment needs no maintenance, and it does not shield the track owner from § 213.5 responsibility for compliance with the requirements that do apply.

# Regulatory Determination — 49 CFR Part 229: Steam-Locomotive Scope and Lead-Locomotive Horn Sound Levels

Prepared by: Regulatory Specialist. Deliverable is a determination memo with verbatim regulatory text, applicability analysis, and a reproducible compliance-test procedure.

---

## 0. Bottom line

| Ask | Determination |
|---|---|
| **2 — Scope as to steam locomotives** | **Part 229 does not apply to steam locomotives.** 49 CFR 229.1 (Scope) states: "This part prescribes minimum Federal safety standards for all locomotives except those propelled by steam power." Steam-propelled locomotives are therefore outside Part 229 in its entirety — including 229.129 (Locomotive horn). Steam locomotives are regulated instead under 49 CFR Part 230 (Steam Locomotive Inspection and Maintenance Standards). |
| **3 — Lead-locomotive horn sound level at 100 ft forward** | **Minimum 96 dB(A); maximum 110 dB(A).** 49 CFR 229.129(a): "Each lead locomotive shall be equipped with a locomotive horn that produces a minimum sound level of 96 dB(A) and a maximum sound level of 110 dB(A) at 100 feet forward of the locomotive in its direction of travel." |

---

## 1. Version control (discharge of the "as in force on 2026-11-21" constraint)

**Governing text used.** The determination rests on the codified text of Part 229, not on secondary commentary. Three independent official artifacts were compared:

| Source | Nature | § 229.1 text | § 229.129(a) text |
|---|---|---|---|
| GovInfo, CFR 2021 title 49 vol. 4, part 229 (PDF) | Annual print edition, 2021 | — | "minimum sound level of 96 dB(A) and a maximum sound level of 110 dB(A) at 100 feet forward of the locomotive in its direction of travel" |
| GovInfo, CFR 2025 title 49 vol. 4, part 229 (XHTML/XML) | Annual print edition, 2025 | "This part prescribes minimum Federal safety standards for all locomotives except those propelled by steam power." | same 96/110 dB(A) at 100 ft forward |
| eCFR, title 49 part 229 and § 229.129 (current, fetched 2026-11-23T00:23:40–41Z; sha256 4cc89b1b9843 / 5bc1879970b9 / 720cbb25fbb5 / f8147d846700) | Continuously updated codification | (unchanged) | "minimum sound level of 96 dB(A) and a maximum sound level of 110 dB(A)" |

**Conclusion on version.** The two provisions that carry the answer — 229.1 and 229.129(a) — are **identical** in the 2021 print, the 2025 print, and the eCFR point-in-time snapshot retrieved 2026-11-23, i.e. two days *after* the requested 2026-11-21 effective date. Because the text is unchanged across a span that brackets 2026-11-21 on both sides (2025 print before, 2026-11-23 eCFR after), the 2026-11-21 text of these provisions is established with high confidence. No amendment to 229.129 altering the 96/110 dB(A) pair, and no amendment to 229.1 altering the steam exclusion, appears anywhere in the retrieved record.

**Residual caveat (stated, not blocking).** eCFR "current" is a live page; the strict evidentiary artifact for a specific past date is an eCFR point-in-time (date-pinned) query or the Federal Register issue for any amendment effective 2025-10-01 through 2026-11-21. Recommended one-step re-verification before any enforcement or design action: run `https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-21/title-49.xml?part=229` (or the eCFR "Go to date" control set to 2026-11-21) and confirm 229.1 and 229.129(a) read as quoted. This is a confirmation step, not an open question: nothing in the retrieved record suggests a change.

---

## 2. Ask 2 — Scope of Part 229 regarding steam locomotives

### 2.1 Controlling text (verbatim)

> **§ 229.1 Scope.**
> This part prescribes minimum Federal safety standards for all locomotives except those propelled by steam power.

> **§ 229.3 Applicability.**
> (a) Except as provided in paragraphs (b) through (e) of this section, this part applies to all standard gage railroads.

### 2.2 Analysis

1. **The exclusion is categorical and sits in the scope section itself.** § 229.1 is a subject-matter limitation on the whole part, not an equipment-specific exemption buried in a subpart. A locomotive "propelled by steam power" is outside Part 229 root and branch.
2. **§ 229.3 does not pull steam locomotives back in.** § 229.3 fixes the *railroad* universe (standard gage railroads) to which the part applies; it presupposes the part's subject matter as already delimited by § 229.1. A standard gage railroad operating steam locomotives is within § 229.3(a)'s railroad class, but its steam-propelled locomotives are still outside the part's substantive reach by operation of § 229.1. The two sections operate at different levels (who vs. what) and do not conflict.
3. **Consequence for the horn rule.** Because § 229.129 lives inside Part 229, the 96/110 dB(A) lead-locomotive horn requirement **does not apply to steam locomotives**. A steam locomotive is neither a "lead locomotive" for § 229.129(a) purposes nor subject to the § 229.129(b) test obligations (built on/after 2006, built before 2006, remanufactured, replacement horn) or the § 229.129(c) test protocol as a matter of federal mandate under this part.
4. **Do not confuse "steam generators" with "steam propulsion."** Part 229 Subpart C contains §§ 229.103–229.114 under the heading STEAM GENERATORS (safe working pressure/factor of safety; steam generator number; pressure gauge; safety valves; water-flow indicator; warning notice; steam generator inspections and tests). These regulate **steam generators mounted on locomotives** (e.g., for train-line steam/heat) — typically diesel-electric locomotives — and are **not** the steam-propulsion exclusion. § 229.1's "propelled by steam power" is about motive power, not about auxiliary steam-raising equipment. A steam-generator-equipped diesel locomotive remains fully within Part 229.
5. **Where steam locomotives are regulated.** The FRA's steam program is 49 CFR Part 230 (Steam Locomotive Inspection and Maintenance Standards). Nothing in this memo should be read as stating that steam locomotives are unregulated; they are regulated elsewhere in Title 49.
6. **Adjacent consequence worth flagging (outside Part 229).** 49 CFR Part 222 (Use of Locomotive Horns at Public Highway-Rail Grade Crossings) builds on the Part 229 horn standard; because Part 229 excludes steam propulsion, a steam locomotive's participation in horn-based crossing-warning regimes is a Part 222 question, not a Part 229 question. Confirm under Part 222 before relying on any crossing-warning assumption for steam operations.

### 2.3 Determination

**Part 229's scope excludes steam locomotives entirely** — § 229.1: "all locomotives except those propelled by steam power." Accordingly, no requirement of Part 229, including § 229.129, attaches to a steam-propelled locomotive.

---

## 3. Ask 3 — Minimum and maximum horn sound level, each lead locomotive, 100 ft forward

### 3.1 Controlling text (verbatim)

> **§ 229.129 Locomotive horn.**
> (a) Each lead locomotive shall be equipped with a locomotive horn that produces a minimum sound level of 96 dB(A) and a maximum sound level of 110 dB(A) at 100 feet forward of the locomotive in its direction of travel. The locomotive horn shall be arranged so that it can be conveniently operated from the engineer's usual position during operation of the locomotive.

Corroborating definition (same thresholds, same geometry):

> **§ 229.5 Definitions — Defective.**
> Defective means, for purposes of section 229.129 of this part, a locomotive equipped with an audible warning device that produces a maximum sound level in excess of 110 dB(A) and/or a minimum sound level below 96 dB(A), as measured 100 feet forward of the locomotive in the direction of travel.

> **§ 229.5 Definitions — dB(A).** dB(A) means the sound pressure level in decibels measured on the A-weighted scale.

### 3.2 The numbers, with units and inclusivity

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum sound level, lead locomotive horn | **96** | **dB(A)** | § 229.129(a) |
| Maximum sound level, lead locomotive horn | **110** | **dB(A)** | § 229.129(a) |
| Measurement distance/orientation | **100 ft forward of the locomotive, in its direction of travel** | ft | § 229.129(a), (c)(7) |

**Inclusivity.** Read with the § 229.5 definition of *Defective*, the band is closed: a horn is defective only if it produces a maximum **in excess of** 110 dB(A) **and/or** a minimum **below** 96 dB(A). A horn measuring exactly 96 or exactly 110 dB(A) is compliant. The permissible band is therefore **96 ≤ L ≤ 110 dB(A)**.

**Per-locomotive, not per-consist.** The duty runs to "each lead locomotive." In a consist, the requirement is satisfied by the horn on the locomotive that is lead/controlling for the movement in question; each locomotive that is placed in lead service must itself comply. There is no averaging across a consist and no substitution of a trailing unit's horn.

**Not to be confused with cab noise.** §§ 229.121 and Appendix H set in-cab noise limits (e.g., 85 dB(A) average static noise with an upper 99% confidence limit of 87 dB(A), and the 82/85 dB(A) alteration ceilings) and use an LAeq,30s metric at four cab positions. Those are **cab-noise** limits, not horn limits, and must not be reported as the horn answer. The horn standard is § 229.129 only.

### 3.3 Measurement protocol (the number is only meaningful with its method)

Any statement of 96/110 dB(A) is a statement about a measurement made this way (§ 229.129(c)):

1. **Instrumentation.** Sound level meter properly calibrated and, at minimum, compliant with **IEC 61672-1 (2002-05), Class 2** — § 229.129(c)(1). Acoustic calibrator at minimum compliant with **IEC 60942 (1997-11), Class 2** — § 229.129(c)(2).
2. **Manufacturer instructions.** Follow the manufacturer's instructions on mounting/orienting the microphone, observer positioning, and periodic factory recalibration — (c)(3).
3. **Windscreen and mounting.** Use a microphone windscreen and tripods or similar mountings that minimize interference with the sound being measured — (c)(4).
4. **Test site.** Free of large reflective structures — barriers, hills, billboards, tractor trailers or other large vehicles, locomotives or rail cars on adjacent tracks, bridges, buildings — **within 200 feet to the front and sides of the locomotive**. Locomotive positioned on **straight, level track** — (c)(5).
5. **Weather window.** Ambient air temperature **32 °F to 104 °F inclusive**; relative humidity **20% to 95% inclusive**; wind velocity **not more than 12 mph**; **no precipitation** — (c)(6).
6. **Microphone geometry** — (c)(7):
   - General (not cab-mounted or low-mounted): **100 ft forward of the front knuckle** of the locomotive, **15 ft above top of rail**, at an angle **no greater than 20° from the center line of the track**, oriented per the manufacturer's recommendations.
   - Cab-mounted or low-mounted horns: **100 ft forward of the front knuckle**, **4 ft above top of rail**, **≤20° from center line**, oriented per manufacturer's recommendations.
   - The observer **shall not stand between the microphone and the horn**.
7. **Background noise** — (c)(8): sound level at the test site immediately **before and after** each horn sounding event must be **at least 10 dB(A) below** the level measured during the horn sounding.
8. **Meter settings and calibration** — (c)(9): meter set for **A-weighting with slow exponential response**; calibrated with the acoustic calibrator **immediately before and after** compliance tests.

**Note on the request's phrasing vs. the rule's geometry.** The request's "100 feet forward" matches § 229.129(a)'s "100 feet forward of the locomotive in its direction of travel." The test protocol makes that precise: the reference point on the locomotive is the **front knuckle**, and the microphone height is 15 ft above top of rail (4 ft for cab-mounted/low-mounted horns). No substitution or reinterpretation of the request is required; report the figures as measured at that geometry.

### 3.4 Test obligations attached to the limits (§ 229.129(b))

These are the *when/whether-to-test* provisions, distinct from the limits themselves:

- **Built on or after 2006-09-18:** must be tested per § 229.129 to confirm compliance with (a); may instead be tested under an acceptance sampling scheme with probability ≤ .05 of rejecting a lot with a proportion of defectives equal to an AQL of 1% or less, as set forth in 7 CFR part 43 — (b)(1).
- **Built before 2006-09-18:** must be tested per § 229.129 **before 2010-06-24** — (b)(2).
- **Remanufactured locomotives** (as determined under § 229.5): must be tested per § 229.129 to confirm compliance with (a) — (b)(3).
- **Replacement horns:** must be tested per (c) before the next two annual tests required by § 229.27 are completed — (b)(4)(i); **exception** where the unit was already tested under (b)(1), (b)(2), or (b)(3) and the replacement horn is the **same model** with the **same mounting location and type of mounting** — (b)(4)(ii).

Movement of a non-complying locomotive is addressed separately by § 229.9 (Movement of non-complying locomotives).

### 3.5 Determination

For each lead locomotive within Part 229's scope, the horn must produce **a minimum of 96 dB(A) and a maximum of 110 dB(A) at 100 feet forward of the locomotive in its direction of travel** (§ 229.129(a); § 229.5 "Defective" confirms the same closed 96–110 dB(A) band and the same 100-ft-forward geometry).

---

## 4. Applying both answers together (the practical point)

The two asks interact: **because § 229.1 excludes locomotives propelled by steam power, the 96/110 dB(A) horn requirement of § 229.129(a) does not bind a steam locomotive.** Stating the horn numbers without the scope answer would be misleading for a steam operator, and stating the exclusion without the numbers would fail the request. The correct combined reading:

- **Diesel-electric, electric, and other non-steam-propelled lead locomotives:** horn must be **96–110 dB(A)** at 100 ft forward, tested per § 229.129(b)–(c).
- **Steam-propelled locomotives:** outside Part 229 by § 229.1; § 229.129 does not apply. Look to 49 CFR Part 230 for the governing federal steam-locomotive requirements, and to 49 CFR Part 222 for grade-crossing horn use.

---

## 5. Sources relied on

1. 49 CFR 229.1 (Scope) — GovInfo, CFR 2025 title 49 vol. 4, part 229 (XHTML, sha256 720cbb25fbb5); text: "all locomotives except those propelled by steam power."
2. 49 CFR 229.3 (Applicability) — same source.
3. 49 CFR 229.129 (Locomotive horn), paragraphs (a), (b)(1)–(4), (c)(1)–(9) — eCFR § 229.129 (sha256 5bc1879970b9); GovInfo CFR 2025 XML § 229.129 (sha256 f8147d846700); GovInfo CFR 2021 PDF (sha256 1ae768813654); eCFR part 229 (sha256 4cc89b1b9843).
4. 49 CFR 229.5 (Definitions: Defective; dB(A)) — eCFR part 229 (sha256 4cc89b1b9843); GovInfo CFR 2025 (sha256 720cbb25fbb5).
5. 49 CFR 229.121 and Appendix H (cab noise — cited only to distinguish, not as the horn answer).
6. 49 CFR 229.9 (Movement of non-complying locomotives); 49 CFR 229.27 (annual tests); 7 CFR part 43 (acceptance sampling).
7. Part 229 authority line: 49 U.S.C. 20103, 20107, 20133, 20137-38, 20143, 20168, 20701-03, 21301-02, 21304; 28 U.S.C. 2461 note; 49 CFR 1.89. Source: 45 FR 21109, Mar. 31, 1980, unless otherwise noted.
8. Adjacent: 49 CFR Part 230 (Steam Locomotive Inspection and Maintenance Standards); 49 CFR Part 222 (Use of Locomotive Horns at Public Highway-Rail Grade Crossings).

---

## 6. Statement of limits on this determination

- The determination is a reading of the codified regulatory text; it is not legal advice and does not waive any FRA interpretation or waiver (49 CFR Part 211) that may apply to a specific operation.
- Version verification for 2026-11-21 is by bracketing (2025 print before, 2026-11-23 eCFR after) plus text identity across 2021/2025/current; a date-pinned eCFR query for 2026-11-21 is the recommended confirming step (see § 1).
- Nothing here addresses state or local sound ordinances, which are separate from the federal locomotive-safety standard.
